title: Visualizing Proteins and Macromolecular Complexes by Negative Stain EM: from Grid Preparation to Image Acquisition
protocol: Fill a large glass beaker with distilled water.
Use a glass pipette to drop a single drop of collodion (~20 μl, 2% in amyl acetate) on the surface of the water.
Place EM grids onto the plastic layer floating on the water surface, one by one in a close packing pattern with the shiny side facing down.
Cut a piece of paper slightly larger than the area where grids are placed.
Carefully place the paper on top of the grid.
Wait until the paper becomes completely wet.
Rapidly make incisions on the plastic film around and close to the soaked paper.
Use a pair of forceps to pick up the paper with the grids sandwiched between the plastic film and paper.
Place the paper in a petri dish with the grids facing up for air drying.
Sharpen a carbon rod using a sharpener.
Load carbon rods in carbon coating machine.
Place one sharpened rod with a sharp tip and another with a flat end against each other.
Apply vacuum grease on half of the frosted area of a glass slide.
Place the glass slide next to the grids on the stage of the carbon coating machine.
Pump the vacuum chamber.
Wait until the vacuum reaches a level of 10-5 Torr.
Increase the current very slowly.
Stop increasing current when the coating starts.
Turn the current off to stop coating when desired thickness has been achieved.
Vent the vacuum chamber.
Remove coated grids for later use.
Weigh out 37.5 mg of uranyl formate into a small beaker.
Add 5 ml of boiling water and stir for 5 minutes in the dark.
Add 10 μl of 5M NaOH, continue stirring for 5 minutes.
Filter the solution using a syringe filter (Fisherbrand, 13mm syringe filter, 0.2μm, Nylon non-sterile).
Store the filtered solution in an 8ml Falcon tube covered with aluminum foil.
Glow-discharge carbon-coated grid using PELCO easiGlow GlowDischarge system.
Set current used for glow discharge to 15 mA.
Glow-discharge grids for 30 seconds.
Use glow-discharged grids shortly after the process, preferably within less than two hours.
Place two 20 μl drops of distilled water on parafilm.
Place two 25 μl drops of uranyl formate solution on parafilm.
Hold a glow-discharged grid using reverse-force anti-capillary forceps with the carbon-coated side facing up.
Apply 2 μl protein sample to the glow-discharged grid.
Wait for 30 seconds.
Blot off the sample using filter paper.
Touch the grid surface to the first drop of water and blot off the water with filter paper.
Repeat with the second drop of water.
Touch the grid surface to the first drop of stain briefly.
Blot off the stain solution with filter paper.
Touch the grid surface to the second drop of stain for 20 seconds.
Blot off the stain solution with filter paper.
Dry the grid using a vacuum.
Briefly check the alignment of the microscope before inserting the sample.
Load the EM grid in the single tilt standard specimen holder.
Insert the holder into CompuStage of the T12.
Wait for the pumping cycle to complete.
Insert the holder into column.
Focus the specimen and set a desired defocus, usually -1.5um.
Record an image using CCD camera.
Search the grid to locate a good area for imaging.
Place two drops (~25 μl) of distilled water and two drops of uranyl formate solution in a piece of parafilm.
Hold a glow discharged carbon-coated EM grid with carbon side up using anti-capillary forceps.
Place a drop of sample (~2 μl) on the grid.
Wait for 30 seconds, then blot the solution with a filter paper.
Flip the grid to touch the sample side of the grid with the first drop of water.
Repeat blottting and flipping steps as necessary to complete the staining process.
